events.name: The Relic Tree
events.intro: An old tree stands alone in a clearing, so old its bark has gone silver. Three seeds hang from its lowest branch: one warm as a coal, one green and soft, one cool and beaded with water. A plaque at its foot, worn almost smooth: "Choose a branch. It grows with you, and it bends to you." An old woman sits on the roots with a flask of tea. Old Merrin, the keeper: "Pick one. The other two go back to sleep. That's how the tree's always been."

success.text: The Ember Seed drops into your palm, warm as a held hand. Merrin nods. "Fire, then. It grows when you're brave in the heat: a fire lit, a beacon, a battle in the sun. Give it to whoever carries your fire." The other two seeds close up, quietly, and go to sleep.

effects.text: You took the Ember Seed from the Relic Tree.

success.text: The Leaf Seed drops into your palm and you swear it breathes. Merrin smiles. "Leaf. That one grows when you mend things: plant, rebuild, feed the hungry. It heals a little better, too." The other two seeds close up, quietly, and go to sleep.

effects.text: You took the Leaf Seed from the Relic Tree.

success.text: The Tide Seed drops into your palm, cold and wet, and you can hear the sea in it. Merrin taps it. "Tide. It grows on the water: rescues, songs, the deep. Mind it near the sea." The other two seeds close up, quietly, and go to sleep.

effects.text: You took the Tide Seed from the Relic Tree.

events.name: Ruined Shrine
events.intro: A shrine fallen in on itself: broken walls, a cracked altar, ivy over all of it. Pieces of an old relic lie scattered in the grass like dropped teeth, and your seed stirs in your bag when you step near them. Someone once kept this place. Nobody has for a long time.

success.text: You pick the pieces out of the grass, one by one. Most are dead stone. One is warm, like your seed. You pocket it.

You set the fallen stones back, as near as you can guess, and clear the ivy off the altar. It takes the afternoon. When the last stone sits true the altar glows, faintly, as if it remembers being thanked. Two pieces are warm now, not one.
You leave the shrine to the ivy. Some things are allowed to stay broken.

events.name: Fragment Dig Site
events.intro: A dig site cut into a hillside, all string lines and little flags. A girl in a hat too big for her sits on an upturned bucket, sorting shards. Tuppence, the digger: "You've got a seed, haven't you? I can tell, they make the shards hum. Collect three pieces and the forge'll do the rest."

success.text: You dig beside her until your arms ache. She talks the whole time, about her gran who dug here first. Near sundown your trowel finds a shard that hums. Tuppence claps. "Told you."
She counts out the change very carefully. "Honest price. Gran said always honest price, because the hill's watching." She gives you the best one.
You tip your hat to her. She tips hers back, and it falls over her eyes.

events.name: The Relic Forge
events.intro: A smith's forge in a stone shed, hot enough to feel from the road. A broad man with burn-scarred forearms looks up from the anvil. Hallam, the smith: "Bring me three fragments and I'll fuse them into your relic. One rule: I only forge the line you chose."

success.text: Hallam turns your three pieces over in his tongs and shakes his head. "Your line's asleep. There's nothing for these to join." He gives you the scrap price for them.

branches.text: Hallam lays the three pieces in the coals and works the bellows until the shed roars. Then he holds your Ember relic beside them, and the pieces run into it like water finding its level. It comes out of the quench a little heavier. "There. It's grown a step. Feel it?" You do.

Hallam lays the three pieces in the coals and works the bellows until the shed roars. Then he holds your Tide relic beside them, and the pieces run into it like water finding its level. It comes out of the quench a little heavier. "There. It's grown a step. Feel it?" You do.

success.text: "Shut for this run," says Hallam. "Once a seed's chosen the other two sleep till the road's done. That's not my rule; it's the tree's." He goes back to the anvil.
You leave Hallam to his fire. The hammering follows you down the road.

events.name: The Relic Shrine
events.intro: Three relics on a stone table in a shrine with no roof, under an open sky. A carved line runs along the table's edge: "Each gift has its price. You may take one." Two of them are finished, crowned and glowing. The third, your own line, is only a sketch carved in the stone: it is not grown yet, and here it never will be.

success.text: You reach for a crown and your hand stops on its own, as if the stone holds it. Your seed is asleep; there is nothing here to trade.

branches.text: You take the Tide crown. It is light, and finished, and it is yours now. In your bag your Ember relic goes grey and dry, all at once, like a leaf in autumn. Everything you grew in it is gone. You hold the dead thing for a while before you put it away.

effects.text: You traded your Ember relic for a finished Tide crown.

effects.text: You traded your Tide relic for a finished Leaf crown.

success.text: You leave the crowns where they lie. The shrine is quiet. Nothing happens, and that is its own answer.

branches.text: You leave the crowns where they lie. On the way out your Ember relic grows warm in your bag, warmer than it has ever been, as if it knows what you did not take.
You leave the crowns where they lie. On the way out your Leaf relic grows warm in your bag, warmer than it has ever been, as if it knows what you did not take.

success.text: Under the carved line, smaller, cut by a different hand: "Whatever you've grown, you lose." Someone has scratched a tally beside it. Most of the marks are old.

events.name: The Relic Tree: Ember Bough
events.intro: The Relic Tree again, or one just like it. Your Ember relic pulls toward it, and when you hold it up, it has grown: a seed no longer, but a small bough, leaves and all. "Your seed has grown a bough." Old Merrin is there, on the roots, with her flask: "Look at that. You've been busy."

success.text: You put your hand on the silver bark and say it out loud, feeling foolish, then not. The bough grows warm. Your Ember relic is twice what it was, and your fire-type leans into your side the whole way back to the road.
You nod to Merrin and keep walking. The bough settles in your relic all the same: it is twice what it was.

events.name: The Relic Tree: Ember Crown
events.intro: The bough on your Ember relic has flowered overnight. "The branch blooms into a crown." Old Merrin turns it over in her hands, and she is crying a little, and does not hide it. "I haven't seen a crown in forty years. Forty years. My mother wore the last one."

success.text: You take the crown back from her, carefully. It is yours. Its holder can't be burned now. Merrin wipes her eyes on her sleeve and laughs at herself.

effects.text: Your Ember relic bloomed into a crown.

success.text: You hold the crown up to the lowest branch and let go. The tree takes it back. Every leaf in the clearing turns over at once, silver side up, and a warm wind goes through the whole party: every hurt closes, every tired face lifts. Merrin cannot speak. She just holds your hand. Your relic stays a bough, and it stays yours.

effects.text: You gave the Ember crown back to the Relic Tree.
